detection.label: Segmentation mask: Model prediction
detection.note: U-Net prediction on the supplied VV/VH decibel bands, thresholded at 0.8 (selected on whole validation scenes). A whole scene is not a training patch: the patch-scale operating point over-predicts at scene scale, so the scene-scale threshold is preferred when it has been measured.

slick.confidenceBasis: mean predicted oil probability over the slick's pixels; this is the model's own output, not a calibrated probability that the feature is oil
qualityFlags: touches the scene edge, so the slick may continue beyond the image
the traced outline self-intersects, so it is published for display only; pixel-based area and shape statistics are unaffected because they are not derived from the outline

screening.label: accepted
screening.headline: consistent with an oil film
reasons: darkness against local water 3.09 background standard deviations — consistent with oil (fitted oil regions average 2.79, rejected regions 1.35)
darkness of the darkest tenth 4.44 background standard deviations — consistent with oil (fitted oil regions average 4.65, rejected regions 2.41)
solidity 0.81 area / convex hull area — consistent with oil (fitted oil regions average 0.62, rejected regions 0.56)
screening.calibration: fitted on 11623 dark regions (930 over labelled oil, 10693 not)
screening.basis: a seven-feature linear screen over shape, texture and darkness statistics; it does not name the phenomenon and it is not a calibrated probability
screening.appliedTo: a component the segmentation network produced, screened by a model fitted on regions a darkness threshold proposed

slick.areaMethod: pixel counts are integrated row by row on a sphere of radius 6371008.8 m, because a degree of longitude shortens with latitude and a single pixel-area constant would bias every scene

screening.headline: 24 dark patches proposed, 24 rejected as more consistent with a look-alike than oil; every one of them lies inside a published slick, so what is rejected here is how the darkness threshold cut that slick up, not the detection

components.note: the same screen applied to what the segmentation network published. The patch counts above are darkness proposals over the whole scene, cut by a threshold rather than by the network, so the two sets of verdicts can disagree about the same water

limits: the screen separates oil-like from not-oil-like; it cannot name the phenomenon, so a rejected patch is never called algae, low wind or a wake
a patch that falls between the two thresholds is returned as uncertain and kept: suppressing a detection the screen is unsure of would trade a measured false positive for an unmeasured missed spill

these patches are darkness proposals, not detections. A rejected patch that overlaps no published slick was never in this case to begin with -- it is evidence about what the screen would have thrown out, not a correction to the 9 slicks above

forcing.rule: CMEMS currents are used only when the product covers the scene in space and its nearest timestep is within the stated tolerance of the acquisition; otherwise the forcing is synthetic and labelled as such

reasons: nearest product time is 3390.9 days from the acquisition, beyond the 24 h tolerance

wind.rule: ERA5 10 m wind is used only when the file covers the scene footprint and its nearest hour is within tolerance of the acquisition; otherwise the wind is synthetic on the synthetic path and omitted on the CMEMS path
reasons: no ERA5 wind file was found on disk (see docs: SPILLTRACE_ERA5 or data/raw/era5_wind*.nc)

forcing.label: Drift forcing: Synthetic scenario data
reasons: nearest product time is 3390.9 days from the acquisition, beyond the 24 h tolerance

forcing.label: Drift forcing: Synthetic scenario data
forcing.method: surface current is the curl of a streamfunction made of three travelling modes at the M2, K1 and M4 tidal periods over a steady background drift, so the flow is analytically non-divergent

amplitudeAnchor.source: CMEMS product, measured over this scene's footprint
amplitudeAnchor.note: the magnitude is taken from the real product even though its timestep does not match the acquisition; only the scale is borrowed, not the flow pattern

wind.note: a uniform wind vector rotating on a fixed period, drawn from the scene's own seed; plausible in magnitude and invented in direction

forcing.windNote: oil also moves at 3% of a synthetic 5.6 m/s wind, i.e. 0.168 m/s, comparable to the 0.072 m/s current - as it is in reality, where wind drift often dominates

landMask.source: CMEMS no-data cells (land is where both velocity components are NaN)
landMask.caveat: the mask is 9.3 km per cell while the imagery is 10 m per pixel, so beaching is detected only to that resolution and a particle within one cell of the coast may already be ashore
landMask.validity: coastlines do not move between the acquisition dates and the product date, so this mask is used even though the currents are not

forcing.reproducibility: seed 3210644435, derived by SHA-256 from the scene identifier and base seed 26143, so the field is identical on every run
forcing.warning: the current field is a plausible synthetic ocean, not the ocean on the acquisition date; trajectories are a methodology demonstration and are not evidence about any real event

releaseWindow.basis: the span covered by the backward drift run: oil seen at the acquisition could have entered the water at any time within it

spillAge.label: Estimated spill age: up to 24 h at acquisition
spillAge.basis: the 24 h backward-drift horizon: oil seen at the acquisition could have entered the water at any time within it

resolution.test: a lookback is distinguishable from the acquisition when the estimated position has moved more than 1 P90 radius from the observed centroid
resolution.note: The hindcast cannot narrow this further. Over the whole run the estimated position of the oil moves less than the P90 radius of the uncertainty around it, so every release time inside the window is equally consistent with this one image.

narrowedBy: a second acquisition of the same area, which fixes the drift actually observed rather than the drift modelled
licensed metocean currents and winds for this scene and these hours, replacing the synthetic forcing
an earlier acquisition showing the area clear of oil, which bounds the age from below directly
spillAge.caveat: The interval is bounded by the drift horizon, not measured. It inherits every limitation of the forcing it was computed from.

originEstimate.interpretation: the centre of the plausible origin region for the observed slick, 24 h before the acquisition

trafficFiltering.rule: A vessel is relevant only if the same AIS report satisfies both halves of the test: it falls inside the estimated release window, and it lies within 3 drift-envelope radii of where the oil is estimated to have been at that report's own timestamp. Everything else is irrelevant traffic: present in the scene, but not near the oil when the oil was there.
trafficFiltering.retentionNote: Excluded vessels are still scored and retained, ranked below the relevant ones, so that the filter itself can be audited. Filtering here means separating the traffic that can support a release from the traffic that cannot, not deleting records.
trafficFiltering.summary: 987 AIS reports · 10 vessels → 9 with reports in the release window → 2 intersect the origin envelope (within 3 envelope radii) → 8 excluded as irrelevant traffic

attributionMethod.distance: great-circle distance to the drift envelope centre at the vessel's own timestamp, full marks inside 1 envelope radii and zero beyond 3
attributionMethod.time: half for being within reach of the estimated oil position during the release window, half scaling to 6 h of such coverage
attributionMethod.trajectory: two thirds for intersecting the envelope, one third for a course across the drift axis, both gated on proximity
attributionMethod.behaviour: full marks below 1 kn near the closest approach, partial for a relative drop
attributionMethod.type: category relevance to bulk oil carriage
attributionMethod.dataCompleteness: 60% report completeness, 40% field completeness, penalised for rejected rows

attributionCaveat: This ranking is a triage aid computed from synthetic AIS and synthetic drift forcing. It is not evidence, it does not establish responsibility, and every entry requires human verification against licensed AIS and observed metocean data.

patchScale.basis: 128 px patches sampled from the scenes, half of them oil-centred

threshold.reason: chosen on the validation split by maximising iou; the full sweep is recorded alongside so the trade-off is visible

baseline.method: despeckled VV, threshold at a calibrated decibel offset below a clean-water reference, morphological opening and a minimum-area filter

train.rule: positives only; the cache holds more oil-bearing patches than the budget

val.rule: positives only; the cache holds more oil-bearing patches than the budget

test.rule: every oil-bearing patch kept; negatives thinned at random to fit

protocol.splitGrouping: train/val/test are assigned by parent Sentinel-1 acquisition, so no crop of one product appears in more than one split
protocol.normalisationSource: training split patches only, invalid pixels excluded

thresholdSelection.reason: chosen on the validation split by maximising iou; the full sweep is recorded alongside so the trade-off is visible

protocol.invalidPixels: excluded from the loss and from every reported metric

limitations: Every supplied scene contains labelled oil, so these figures measure delineation quality on scenes already known to contain a slick; they are not a false-alarm rate on clean sea.
The dataset contains no labelled look-alikes (algal blooms, low-wind zones, rain cells, ship wakes), so the model's ability to reject them is untested and unquantified here.
Metrics are computed on 128 px patches sampled from the scenes rather than on whole 2048 px scenes, so they do not include errors that only appear at scene scale.
The reference masks are the supplied labels; their own accuracy is unknown and is treated as ground truth throughout.

sceneScale.basis: Whole-scene evaluation at 2048x2048. The patch metrics in metrics.json are measured on 128 px crops sampled around labelled oil and therefore do not include the false positives that only appear at scene scale.
sceneScale.thresholdSelection: chosen on the validation scenes by mean per-scene IoU, then applied unchanged to the test scenes
limitations: Every supplied scene contains labelled oil, so these figures still measure delineation on scenes known to contain a slick and are not a false-alarm rate on clean sea.
Scene-scale IoU is markedly lower than patch-scale IoU because the patch sampler never visited most of each frame; the scene figure is the one that reflects operating on a full acquisition.
The reference masks are the supplied labels and are treated as ground truth; their own accuracy is unknown.

lookAlike.question: Given a dark region in a SAR scene, is it oil or a look-alike? Every other metric in this project assumes the answer is already oil.

features.name: darknessZ
features.label: darkness against local water
features.rationale: oil damps the short capillary waves the radar sees, so a film sits several standard deviations below the water around it; a low-wind patch is shallower because the water is only slightly smoother, not covered

features.name: darknessP10Z
features.label: darkness of the darkest tenth
features.rationale: a mean can be dragged down by a few very dark pixels, so the tenth percentile asks whether the whole region is dark or only part of it

features.name: textureRatio
features.label: interior roughness
features.rationale: a damped surface is smoother than the sea around it, so its pixel spread is narrower; wind shadows and blooms stay as speckled as open water

features.name: edgeSharpness
features.label: edge definition
features.rationale: a film has a physical boundary and the backscatter steps across it; a low-wind zone fades, so its edge gradient is no stronger than the ambient texture

features.name: compactness
features.label: compactness
features.rationale: spills are drawn out by wind and current into ragged forms; a compact blob is more consistent with a wind cell or a bloom patch

features.name: solidity
features.label: solidity
features.rationale: a slick feathers at its edges and leaves gaps inside its hull; a smooth convex region is a weaker candidate

features.name: elongation
features.label: elongation
features.rationale: a discharge from a moving vessel is linear, and wind stretches any film along its axis, so elongation argues for oil -- though a ship wake is linear too, which is why this feature is never decisive on its own

trainedOn.labelRule: a dark region counts as oil when the supplied reference mask covers >= 50% of it and as not-oil when it covers <= 5%; the rest are dropped rather than guessed at
trainedOn.proposerNote: the proposer is the same code that runs on the look-alike set and is given no reference mask; its recall of the labelled oil is reported so a high screening score cannot hide a proposer that simply missed the slick

limitations: The look-alike labels in the same-domain half are the absence of oil in the supplied reference mask, not a positive identification of a phenomenon. A dark region the mask does not cover may be low wind, a wake, an unlabelled slick, or a labelling error.

The screen decides between oil and a look-alike for a region that has already been proposed. It cannot recover a slick the proposer never found, and its sensitivity is therefore conditional on the proposer, not on the sea.

A region the screen calls uncertain stays in the case. That is deliberate for a response tool -- suppressing an unsure detection would trade a measured false positive for an unmeasured missed spill -- but it means the rejection rate is the rate of outright rejections and not one minus the acceptance rate.

The screen was fitted on 270 parent products; a linear model over seven features on that many independent sites is a screen, not a classifier of phenomena, and it deliberately never names which look-alike it thinks it is looking at.

The look-alike patches are 8-bit JPEG at about 20 m/pixel from a different sea. They are resampled to this project's ground sampling before scoring and every model feature is a ratio of same-unit quantities, so the comparison is defensible -- but the unpublished greyscale stretch remains an untested assumption behind the invariance claim.

126 of 2290 look-alike patches produced no dark region at all, so the proposer -- not the screen -- is what rejected them. They are counted in the patch rate and absent from the region rate, which is why both are reported.

The detector's false-alarm rate is indicative, not a published figure. An 8-bit JPEG cannot be turned back into calibrated decibels and the archive is single-channel, so the second polarisation is synthesised from the first and is perfectly correlated with it. Two mappings are reported precisely because one number would overstate what the data supports.

limits: AIS traffic is synthetic. No real vessel appears anywhere in this product.
Drift forcing is synthetic unless the CMEMS product covers the scene in both space and time; the mode is stated on every screen that uses it.
Rankings are triage aids. Nothing here establishes responsibility for a discharge.
Segmentation accuracy is measured on held-out patches from the supplied dataset only, grouped by parent acquisition; it is not a field-validated detection rate.
Look-alike screening separates oil-like from not-oil-like. It does not identify the phenomenon, so no rejected patch is called algae, low wind or a wake.
